name: Highway 413 (GTA West Corridor) — Construction Start
proponent: Government of Ontario / Ministry of Transportation
summary: Ontario's 2026 Budget (released March 26, 2026) confirmed construction has started on the 52-km Highway 413, a new 400-series highway connecting Highways 400, 410, 427, and 400 in the Greater Toronto Area. The 2026 construction season is focused on Bovaird Drive and Highway 10 underpasses. The project is part of Ontario's $210 billion 10-year capital plan.

name: QEW Garden City Skyway Bridge Twinning — New Bridge over Welland Canal
proponent: Government of Ontario / Ministry of Transportation
summary: Ontario's 2026 Budget (released March 26, 2026) confirmed advance works commenced in winter 2026 on the twinning of the Garden City Skyway Bridge over the Welland Canal on the Queen Elizabeth Way. The project adds a second bridge span to address capacity constraints on the QEW corridor connecting the Niagara region to the Greater Toronto Area.

name: Ontario Hospital Infrastructure Program — 50 Hospital Projects ($64B, 10-Year)
summary: Ontario Budget 2026 (March 26, 2026) committed $64 billion in health infrastructure over 10 years, supporting 50 hospital projects and the addition of 3,000 new hospital beds across the province. The commitment is part of Ontario's $210 billion 10-year capital plan and represents the largest healthcare infrastructure commitment in the province's history.

name: Trans-Canada Highway Twinning — Manitoba to Ontario Border
summary: Manitoba's 2026 Budget (released March 24, 2026) committed $3.8 billion in capital investments, with the Trans-Canada Highway twinning to the Ontario border identified as a priority project. The budget also includes $22 million for the Red-Seine-Rat East Water and Wastewater Treatment Network, $22 million for the Pembina Valley Water Co-op, and highway upgrades to PTH 2 and the Deloraine-Winchester Airport.

name: Manitoba Health Centre Construction — Portage la Prairie, Neepawa, Brandon, Winkler/Morden, Thompson
summary: Manitoba's 2026 Budget (released March 24, 2026) funded construction and expansion of health centres in five communities: Portage la Prairie, Neepawa, Brandon, Winkler/Morden, and Thompson. The health centre investments are included in the province's $3.8 billion capital program announced in the budget.

name: Quebec City Tramway — Preferred Bidders Selected for Two Major Contracts
proponent: Réseau de transport de la Capitale (RTC) / Government of Quebec
summary: In March 2026, Quebec City Tramway (TramCité) selected two preferred bidders — consortia Tram Alliance and Quebec Connexion Capitale — for major construction contracts. Active construction is underway on a 5-km span between Université Laval and Grand Théâtre. The full tramway is scheduled to commence operations in 2033. The project is part of Quebec's $167 billion 10-year capital infrastructure plan.

name: LNG Canada Phase 2 — Capacity Expansion, Kitimat
proponent: LNG Canada (Shell Canada, PETRONAS, PetroChina, Mitsubishi, Korea Gas)
summary: LNG Canada Phase 2 would double export capacity at the Kitimat, BC facility from 14 million tonnes per annum to 28 Mt/y. Coastal GasLink Phase 2 pipeline agreements are advancing. The proposed expansion is referenced in PM Carney's $5.6 billion energy and critical minerals package. Phase 1 loaded its first cargo for export in June 2025 and marine terminal in-water works are scheduled to commence April 15, 2026.

name: Ksi Lisims LNG Terminal — Nisga'a Territory, BC
proponent: Western LNG / Nisga'a Nation / Rockies LNG Partners
summary: Ksi Lisims LNG is Canada's proposed second-largest LNG export facility, located in Nisga'a territory in northwestern British Columbia. The project would liquefy natural gas from BC's Montney formation for export to Asia. The project is referenced in BC's 2026 capital projects summary and in PM Carney's northern energy development package announced in the March 24-30 window.

name: Mackenzie Highway Extension — Yellowknife to Inuvik All-Season Road
proponent: Government of Canada / Government of Northwest Territories
summary: PM Carney's March 12, 2026 announcement of a $35 billion Arctic defence and northern infrastructure plan includes an all-season Mackenzie Highway extension connecting Yellowknife to Inuvik, Northwest Territories. The highway would open the Mackenzie Valley corridor to year-round surface access, supporting resource development and Arctic sovereignty. The project is part of the Arctic Economic and Security Corridor initiative.

name: Build Canada Homes — National Federal Housing Program ($13B)
proponent: Government of Canada / Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation
summary: The federal Build Canada Homes program commits $13 billion over five years to construct homes on six federally owned sites across Canada. The program targets 4,000 homes on surplus federal land. The federal-Ontario cost-matched agreement, signed in March 2026, includes up to 50% reductions in municipal development charges and the removal of HST on new homes valued up to $1 million for municipalities representing approximately 80% of Ontario's population.

name: Alberta APMC Northern Pipeline Corridor — BC Coast
summary: Alberta's 2026 Budget authorized $900 million in borrowing authority for the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission to explore and potentially develop a new oil pipeline corridor to the northern British Columbia coast. The initiative responds to TMX operating near full capacity and aims to open additional Pacific export routes for Alberta crude. Budget released March 2026.

name: Protect Ontario Account Investment Fund
summary: Ontario's 2026 Budget (March 26, 2026) established a $4 billion Protect Ontario Account Investment Fund targeting foreign direct investment in AI, defence, advanced manufacturing, and life sciences. The budget also added $600 million to the existing Invest Ontario Fund. The combined $4.6 billion in new investment incentive capital is positioned to attract manufacturing and technology projects in response to US tariff disruptions.

name: Quebec Critical Minerals and Economic Transformation Package — $1.7B
summary: Quebec's 2026-27 Budget (March 25 session) allocated $1.7 billion over five years to accelerate economic transformation, including $480 million for critical and strategic minerals development and cultural content investment. The minerals allocation supports mine development and processing capacity in the James Bay and northern Quebec regions, consistent with Quebec's critical minerals strategy.

name: BMO Field Upgrade — Toronto
proponent: Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment / City of Toronto
summary: A $150 million upgrade of BMO Field in Toronto is underway ahead of the FIFA World Cup in June 2026. The redevelopment expands seating capacity and upgrades facilities to meet FIFA standards for the tournament. BMO Field will serve as one of the Canadian host venues for the 2026 World Cup.

name: Grays Bay Road and Port — Nunavut Arctic Coast
proponent: Government of Canada / Kitikmeot Inuit Association
summary: The Grays Bay Road and Port project consists of a 900-km road linking Canada's highway system at Yellowknife to a proposed deepwater port on Nunavut's Arctic coast near the Northwest Passage midpoint. The federal government included the project in the $35 billion Arctic defence and northern infrastructure plan announced March 12, 2026. The port would enable year-round export of critical minerals from the Slave Geological Province.
